texts.preamble: Adani Wilmar Limited vs Central Food Safety Officer on 15 July, 2025 15th July, 2025 (Ak) 09 Cra (Db) 268 of 2025 (F.A.T 216 of 2024) Ia No: Can 1 of 2024 Can 2 of 2024
texts.facts: 1. CAN 1 of 2024 and CAN 2 of 2024 are treated to be on the day's list. 2. CAN 1 of 2024 is an application for condonation of delay in preferring the present appeal under Section 71(6) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'the 2006 Act'). 3.
texts.arguments: Learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant, by placing reliance on the averments made in the condonation application, submits that the delay was occasioned for reasons beyond the control of the appellant. 4. First, the authorized signatory of the appellant, who was well-acquainted with the facts of the case and was in charge of drafting the appeal, was not Adani Wilmar Limited vs Central Food Safety Officer on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174296996/ 1 available at the relevant juncture due to some personal difficulty. 2 5. Subsequently, difficulties cropped up since the Filing Department of this court was itself in some doubt as to what heading the appeal would be classified under. 6. 12. For the present, learned senior counsel confines his arguments to the aspect of the allegation of "misbranding". 16. However, the Appellate Authority, in an appeal preferred by the present appellant against the portion of the Adjudicating Officers' order whereby the sample of the appellant was termed to be sub- standard, traversed beyond its jurisdiction and, apart from affirming the portion of the Adjudicating Officer's order whereby the sample was held to be sub-standard, also entered into the question as to Adani Wilmar Limited vs Central Food Safety Officer on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174296996/ 3 whether there was misbranding and upset the finding of the Adjudication Officer by reversing the same and holding that the sample was 'misbranded' as well. 17. 19. Learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant also points out from the recording in the impugned judgment itself that the respondent-authority appeared and submitted that it relied on the order of the learned Adjudicating Officer and according to the respondent-authority, the said order was legal and valid. 20. Thus, it is argued, the legality and validity of the Adjudicating Officer's order, to the extent that the allegation of 'misbranding' of the appellant's product was turned down, was also accepted by the respondent itself. 21. Upon hearing learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant, we find that there is substance in such contentions of the appellant. 22. First, no appeal was preferred by the respondent- authority against the finding of the Adjudicating Officer turning down the allegation of misbranding of the appellant's product sample and the appellate authority acted prima facie beyond its jurisdiction in suo motu taking up the said aspect and reversing the finding of the Adjudicating Officer.
